title: Semisimple groups generated by integral Chevalley root exponentials
statement:
Let $V,R,\bar c_\alpha,P$ be a reduced rational crystallographic root system and its weight lattice as defined in [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding]. Suppose given a split semisimple rational Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, Cartan algebra $\mathfrak h$, Chevalley basis $h_\delta,e_\alpha$, faithful representation $\rho$ on $W$, weight set $\Omega$ and full weight-decomposed lattice $\Lambda$ satisfying all the displayed Chevalley-basis, nilpotence, integrality and $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$ conditions in [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation]. Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and put $W_F=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbf Z}F$. Write $D_F(A)=\operatorname{Spec}F[A]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $A$, where the group algebra has basis $e^a$, multiplication $e^ae^b=e^{a+b}$, comultiplication $e^a\mapsto e^a\otimes e^a$, counit $e^a\mapsto1$ and antipode $e^a\mapsto e^{-a}$. Let $T=D_F(P)$ act on $(\Lambda\cap W_\lambda)\otimes F$ by its character $\lambda$. For every $\alpha\in R$ the integral matrices $D_{\alpha,m}$ give a group-scheme map $x_\alpha:\mathbf G_a\to\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$ by
$$x_\alpha(a)=\sum_{m\geq0}(D_{\alpha,m}\otimes1)a^m$$
on every commutative $F$-algebra; the sum is finite by nilpotence. The smallest closed algebraic subgroup $H\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$ containing the images of all $x_\alpha$ is smooth, connected and semisimple (no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup). It contains $T$ as a split maximal torus, and its root datum has character lattice $P$, roots $R$ and coroots $\bar c_\alpha\in\operatorname{Hom}(P,\mathbf Z)$, using the group-root conventions of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For $V=0,R=\varnothing$ this gives $H=T=1$. No identification of $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ with a chosen integral Lie-algebra form in positive characteristic is asserted.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153) and Theorem 23.72, printed pp.510--511, with the full-weight representation of Corollary 23.73; torus defined by its weight characters.

proof.text: The given lattice conditions in [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation] make each $D_{\alpha,m}$ an integral endomorphism. Over $\mathbf Q$ one has $D_{\alpha,i}D_{\alpha,j}=\binom{i+j}{i}D_{\alpha,i+j}$, so the equality holds on the torsion-free lattice. Comparing the coefficient of $a^ib^j$ proves $x_\alpha(a)x_\alpha(b)=x_\alpha(a+b)$ over $\mathbf Z[a,b]$ and hence every $F$-algebra. The inverse is $x_\alpha(-a)$. Also $D_{\alpha,m}(W_\lambda)\subset W_{\lambda+m\alpha}$, by the representation bracket $[h,e_\alpha]=\alpha(h)e_\alpha$; therefore $t x_\alpha(a)t^{-1}=x_\alpha(\alpha(t)a)$. These are polynomial identities before reduction; no factorial is inverted in $F$.

source.place: Equation (153), p.510; coefficient calculation written out.

proof.text: Construct the smallest closed subgroup $H$ without presupposing smoothness. Enumerate $R$ and put $f(a)=\prod_{\alpha\in R}x_\alpha(a_\alpha)$. The pointed morphism $\varphi:\mathbf A^{2|R|}\to\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$, $\varphi(a,b)=f(a)f(b)^{-1}$, has inverse-stable image because $\varphi(a,b)^{-1}=\varphi(b,a)$. Its image contains each root map (set all other coordinates to zero), and any subgroup containing the root maps contains its image. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup]. Affine space is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected, so the resulting smallest subgroup $H$ is geometrically reduced, geometrically connected, affine and of finite type. It is smooth by [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth].

source.place: Theorem 23.72, p.510; scheme-theoretic interpretation of generated subgroup using the existing pointed-map construction.

proof.text: The weight action embeds $T$: choose a lattice basis within each weight summand. The map from the character lattice of the diagonal matrix torus to $P$ sends each coordinate to its weight. It is surjective since $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$, so [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] makes the map a closed immersion. Since $P$ is free, [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] identifies $T$ with a split torus and $X^*(T)$ with $P$. By [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans], the simple coroots form a $\mathbf Z$-basis of the lattice generated by all coroots. Its dual is exactly $P$ by the defining integrality conditions, so they are the dual basis of $P$; thus $\prod_{\delta\in\Delta}\mathbf G_m\to T$, $(s_\delta)\mapsto\prod h_\delta(s_\delta)$, is an isomorphism. Each $h_\delta$ lies in $H$: use [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-rank-one] and the explicit identity $\operatorname{diag}(s,s^{-1})=w(s)w(-1)$, where $w(s)=x_+(s)x_-(-s^{-1})x_+(s)$. Hence $T\subset H$ and $H$ is also the subgroup generated by $T$ and all root maps.

source.place: Equation (152) and Theorem 23.72, pp.510-511; torus recovered from its actual weight characters, not all independent diagonal scalars.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-exponential-big-cell] to $K=H$. Its equivariant differential says that the zero-character subspace of $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ is exactly $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$; every other summand has the distinct nonzero character $\alpha\in R$. If a torus $S\subset H$ contains $T$, its tangent space injects into this zero-character subspace, since $S$ commutes with $T$. The smooth-group identities [lem-ag-smooth-lie-local-dimension] and [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] therefore give $\dim S\leq\dim T$. Tori are smooth connected by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus]. A proper closed inclusion of smooth connected groups has strict dimension inequality by [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products]; consequently $S=T$. This proves maximality before any reductive-group theorem is applied. The same differential identifies the full nonzero tangent-character set with $R$.

source.place: Theorem 23.72 proof, pp.510-511: verification of the maximal-torus hypothesis missing from the compressed proof.

proof.text: For $\delta\in\Delta$, [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-rank-one] supplies the split reductive subgroup $J_\delta=\langle T,x_\delta,x_{-\delta}\rangle\subset H$, with roots $\pm\delta$ and maximal torus $T$. Its root subgroups are the images of $x_{\pm\delta}$: by the same lemma $x_{\pm\delta}$ is a closed immersion, so its image is a smooth connected closed subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a$; it is normalized by $T$ by step 1; its tangent line $F\,dx_{\pm\delta}(1)$ is nonzero, since a closed immersion is injective on tangent spaces, and has character $\pm\delta$, so it equals the $\pm\delta$-weight space of $\operatorname{Lie}(J_\delta)$, which is one-dimensional as the tangent space of $U_{\pm\delta}\simeq\mathbf G_a$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] gives $U_{\pm\delta}=x_{\pm\delta}(\mathbf G_a)$. Hence the commutation of $x_{-\delta}$ with $x_\epsilon$ for distinct simple roots, also given by [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-rank-one], is the commutation of $U_{-\delta}$ and $U_\epsilon$ required below. Let $G$ be generated by these $J_\delta$ and $T$. Every $n_\delta$ lies in $G$, and the same lemma expresses every $x_\gamma$ as a conjugate of some simple-root map by a word in the $n_\delta^{\pm1}$. Thus $G$ contains every generator of $H$, while its generators lie in $H$; so $G=H$. The simple roots are $\mathbf Z$-linearly independent by the chosen base. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-rank-one-reductive-generation] now hold in the smooth connected ambient group $H$, with its already maximal torus $T$. The theorem makes $H$ split reductive with simple-root base $\Delta$.

source.place: Theorem 23.31, p.494, and Theorem 23.72 proof, p.511; simple-root generation and all hypotheses supplied explicitly.

proof.text: The open chart already gives the entire root set $R\subset X^*(T)=P$. For any $\alpha\in R$, [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-rank-one] gives the reductive subgroup $J_\alpha\subset H$ with the same maximal torus $T$, roots $\pm\alpha$ and coroot $h_\alpha$. The rank-one compatibility clause of [lem-sfb-rank-one-reductive-generation] identifies this with the coroot of $\alpha$ in $H$. Its pairing with $\lambda\in P$ is $\bar c_\alpha(\lambda)$ by its explicit diagonal formula. Hence the full root datum, including all coroots, is the stated one. The roots span $P\otimes\mathbf Q=V$, so [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span] makes $H$ semisimple in the required smooth connected solvable-normal-subgroup sense. In rank zero $P=0$, all root maps are absent, and the pointed-map construction is the identity subgroup; thus $H=T=1$. No assertion about a reduced integral Lie form was needed.

source.place: Theorem 23.72 and Corollary 23.73, pp.510-511; coroot compatibility from Remark 23.33 and Theorem 21.11, with the root-span semisimplicity criterion.

proof_origin.place: Expanded assembly of Section 23h, equations (152)-(153) and Theorem 23.72; Theorem 23.31 used with its actual maximal-torus hypothesis. Omitted integral rank-one and open-cell details are separate statement-only prerequisites.
